body:
A lockout may be coming, but nobody told the hot stove. It's already burning bright with even the biggest prize, two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, coming off the market. Trevor Rogers and Freddy Peralta soon followed, and with Kevin Gausman and Jazz Chisholm coming off the board over Thanksgiving weekend, most of the marquee free agents are already nailed down.There's a reason for the urgency. Once the lockout becomes official, the signings -- and all other transactions -- will cease, but those that occur before then will still count toward the date when baseball is allowed to resume. So we'd better document them all here, just like any other offseason, breaking down their impact for Fantasy Baseball.         That's what Scott White and Chris Towers intend to do over the next few weeks, at least, before everything goes quiet. They'll eventually pick up where they left off when the hot stove heats up again in ... March? Hopefully not much later than that.         Whatever the timeline, you'll want this page bookmarked so you can get the first word on everything that happens.
Jazz Chisholm signs with Blue JaysThe terms here are complicated. The Blue Jays are for sure paying Chisholm $20 million for one year, signing bonuses and theoretical buyouts included. The deal includes a $16 million player option for 2028 (in case Chisholm struggles) as well as a $40 million team option (in case he thrives). That disparity underscores how volatile of an asset Chisholm has become, though that's probably truer for real life than for Fantasy.

No doubt, his 2026 was a step back from his career-best 2025, when he went 30/30, but he still had 19 homers and 41 steals in 137 games. His combined home run and stolen base total was only two off from 2025, and his batting average slipped only 11 points, from .242 to .231. The biggest change for Fantasy was the drop in RBI, from 80 to 55, but switching teams should reset expectations as far as that goes. Of course, it should probably reset them for the worse given that the Blue Jays ranked dead last in runs scored last year, though their reputation for cultivating hitter talent points to better days ahead. It's true Chisholm's slippage was more evident from a real-world perspective, with his performance against fastballs standing out in particular, but I wouldn't rule out a return to form at age 29. He may not even need one, though, to justify drafting as a top-four second baseman in 2027. --Scott WhiteKevin Gausman signs with TigersYou would think a pitcher entering the twilight of his career at age 36 would hold out for a multi-year deal, but Gausman ultimately had to settle for a one-year, $25 million contract with the Tigers. He's back with the organization where he just spent the past six-plus seasons, agreeing Tuesday to a three-year, $30 million deal with the Reds. He does have an opt out after the first two seasons, and by that point, stud prospect Alfredo Duno may be ready to take over by the plate. This deal permits the soon-to-be 21-year-old the leeway to develop fully. As for Stephenson, we know what to expect from him with the Reds. They play in as favorable of a home run venue as there is, which I suppose makes this signing good news, though Stephenson's home/away splits have run pretty even throughout his career unenticing overall. He's a serviceable enough second catcher for Rotisserie leagues, capable of hitting 15 home runs with a batting average that won't kill you, but unless you get squeezed out at the position, you'd prefer to target someone higher-upside on Draft Day. --Scott White
Kaima Taira signs with Blue JaysIf Taira makes 20 starts in 2027, he'll be just the second pitcher in the past 40 years to do so while listed at 5-foot-8 or below – Marcus Stroman, of course, did it eight times between 2014 and 2024. That alone tells you how unique Taira is. Taira spent much of his career in Japan jumping between the bullpen and the rotation, and he found success as both a closer and, more recently, a frontline starter, coming off a season where he threw 146 innings of 23 starts with a 1.36 ERA. Despite his diminutive size and merely-good 25% strikeout rate, Taira sits in the mid-90s with his fastball, and it plays up even more because he somehow manages to generate 6.8 feet of extension when he releases the ball. As we have come to expect from pitchers coming over from Japan, Taira features a full arsenal, with a slider, cutter, curveball, changeup, and splitter, and he improved his command across the board in 2026 en route to a career-best 7.9% walk rate. After signing for five years and $80 million (with an opt-out after the third season), Taira seems all but certain to open the 2027 season in the Blue Jays rotation. Whether he stays there for good will depend on how he acclimates to the majors, and as Tatsuya Imai showed us last season, that's no guarantee. But Taima has the talent and contract of a major-league starter, and potentially a pretty good one. He's a viable reserve rounds target for 2027 drafts. --Chris Towers  Freddy Peralta signs with Orioles  The Orioles basically swapped out Trevor Rogers for Peralta while getting an extra first-round pick out of the deal, and given that the talent disparity between the two seems pretty minimal, it's a reasonable move. But if the Orioles aren't getting a downgrade in talent, they might be taking on some more volatility and putting a bit more pressure on the bullpen. Rogers has averaged 5.8 innings per start over the past two seasons while Peralta is at 5.3.

The right-hander has long been a volatile pitcher, but 2026 was the first time his ERA ended up on the wrong side of 4.00 since 2019. In 2025, he made 20 starts before his season ended in July with a rotator cuff strain, and then he managed nine starts before a left elbow issue ended his run as a starter in 2026 (he re-emerged in September as a single-inning reliever for the Dodgers).

The Cubs are, for all intents and purposes, swapping out Seiya Suzuki for Sato, but can Sato be as good as Suzuki? The upside is there, but the Cubs are taking on quite a bit of risk in this swap. Sato clearly has power, hitting a combined 79 home runs over the past two seasons, but he also struck out 27% of the time during that time. In contrast, Suzuki never struck out more than 22% of the time while in Japan and yet has run a 25% strikeout rate throughout his major league career. For more, check out my full-length article. --Chris Towers  Trevor Rogers signs with Cubs  Maybe you thought Sonny Gray's two-year, $55 million deal with the Twins was too little. For me, maybe, since I rank him 36th at starting pitcher, but early ADP has him going only 53rd, behind the likes of Nick Pivetta and Christian Scott. It's clear, then, that Fantasy Baseballers, at least the kind that participate in November NFBC drafts, don't regard Rogers as highly as the game at large does. A big reason for that, I think, is that he had an ERA over 4.00 in 2026, which most Roto rating systems regard as an albatross around a pitcher's neck, but perhaps a better indicator of the way he pitched was his 3.45 FIP.

This is a trade that makes a ton of sense for real-life baseball but might be a disaster for Fantasy. The Mariners got -0.5 WAR from their third basemen in 2026, per FanGraphs, and Garcia represents a significant upgrade from that. As recently as 2025, put up a .286/.351/.449 line and was a borderline elite Fantasy option as a result.   Unfortunately for our purposes, this trade makes it a lot less likely he'll live up to that level of play in 2027. Kauffman Stadium in Kansas City suppresses homers but is generally a pretty good offensive environment, sporting the seventh-best park factor for hitters, per BaseballSavant.com. T-Mobile Park in Seattle? It's the worst hitter's park in baseball by a pretty wide margin, though how that impacts each individual hitter often varies. Randy Arozarena more or less held serve in his time in Seattle, while someone like Eugenio Suarez struggled mightily in both stints there. It's something about the way hitters see the ball and how the humid, often chilly atmosphere affects batted balls' trajectories. There just isn't another offensive environment in baseball quite like T-Mobile Park, and it generally serves as a drag on offense across the board.     If Garcia can hit like he did in 2025, he'll still be very fantasy-relevant, however. That season saw Garcia max out his power, bumping his average exit velocity to 91.3 mph, while also increasing his launch angle, allowing him to tap into far more of that power than ever before. That he did it without sacrificing his superlative contact skills made for a very strong package. But he gave back nearly all of those improvements in 2026 and returned to being a roughly average hitter. He struggled while playing through injuries to his left hand and wrist before eventually going on the IL for nearly two months, then struggled with hamstring issues late in the season. If the injuries explain his struggles, then betting on a bounceback makes sense, even in Seattle.     
But 2025 might have just been a career year, and the move to T-Mobile Park makes it even less likely he'll get back to that level. Garcia's price has already slipped to 169.4 in early NFBC drafts, but I'd expect it to drop even farther after this. He's a fringe starting-caliber third baseman for Fantasy, and I'd take at least Curtis Mead and Isaac Paredes ahead of him, among players with a current lower ADP. --Chris Towers          Bryce Miller traded to the Royals  While Maikel Garcia is going to the worst hitter's park in the league, Miller suffers from the opposite move, exiting one of the best pitching environments in the league. It's one he has specifically benefited from, sporting a career 3.49 ERA at home compared to a 4.63 ERA on the road. It would be overly simplistic to say he has lost whatever Fantasy relevance he had with this move, but it might not end up wrong.

It's not the first place I would have bet on Gray signing, but the Twins have made it clear since the most recent trade deadline that they aren't looking to rebuild. The deal is officially for one year but includes a 2028 player option for the 37-year-old Gray, meaning the Twins will either be happy about getting one great season out of him or will be looking at a fairly onerous (but short!) deal for 2028. It's a tradeoff worth making for a team like the Twins, who have talent in the rotation but little in the way of sure things, either from a performance or a health perspective. Gray is seemingly a different type of pitcher every season, but from a real-life perspective, it's easy to see the appeal in employing him: He has made at least 24 starts in every season since 2017 (minus the shortened 2020 season) and has had an ERA over 4.00 just twice in his past eight seasons.   From a Fantasy perspective, his value is a little less clear. He had an excellent 2026 season that saw him take advantage of an elite Red Sox defense to put up a 2.72 ERA. It did, however, come with a huge decrease in his strikeout rate, and that came after two seasons with a combined ERA of 4.07. He's almost always a must-start pitcher, but it often feels like you can't fully trust him. Of course, with an ADP around 150 in early drafts, it doesn't really matter if you can fully trust him. Just roll him out there, hope the ERA is closer to 3.50 than 4.00 and don't overthink it. title: 2026 SEC Championship Game: Texas gets one last shot at Georgia in contest's final edition - CBS Sports
description: The Longhorns earned a shot at the league's last championship game title with a win over rival Texas A&M
body:
The Longhorns earned a shot at the league's last championship game title with a win over rival Texas A&M

        The 35th SEC Championship Game will feature a pair of juggernauts in a budding rivalry dominated by one team.No. 3 Texas clinched its spot with a 16-6 win at Texas A&M on Friday night, setting up a rematch of the 2024 title game against No. 1 Georgia. Kickoff is next Saturday at 4 p.m. ET on ABC.The SEC's title game is not short on storylines. For one, the game is going away starting next season as the College Football Playoff expands to 24 teams in 2027, so both programs are vying to possibly be the final winner of the SEC Championship Game. Secondly, the recent history between Georgia and Texas is deep, and though Georgia has dominated it, Texas might tap its first-year defensive coordinator for invaluable intel to turn the tables.Will Muschamp stood on the Georgia sideline at Mercedes-Benz Stadium two Decembers ago, a co-defensive coordinator in red and black, when the Bulldogs beat Texas 22-19 in overtime for the SEC championship. He was also on Georgia's staff for the two blowout victories since Texas joined the conference.
On Saturday, he'll be on the other sideline, and possibly carrying the intel the Longhorns need to finally crack Georgia's code. The Bulldogs have owned this matchup since Texas arrived in the SEC, going 3-0 against Steve Sarkisian's Longhorns with two double-digit wins. The two haven't met since November 2025, when Georgia handed Texas a 35-10 loss in Athens. Muschamp was hired as Texas' defensive coordinator last December after five seasons on Kirby Smart's staff. No matter the result in Atlanta, the losing team will likely land in the 12-team CFP field.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    What to know about GeorgiaGeorgia is chasing a third straight SEC title, something the program hasn't done since Herschel Walker carried it to three in a row at the start of the 1980s. This is the Bulldogs' sixth straight trip to the title game, a record that may now never be broken. Georgia's only loss this season was a 27-24 home head-scratcher against Auburn. Georgia hasn't been tested since. The Bulldogs beat Florida and Ole Miss on the road, and beat Missouri and South Carolina by a combined score of 151-42. They are scoring 41.2 points per game, tied for third nationally, and have outscored opponents 132-17 in the first quarter.
Stockton has been efficient as ever since that afternoon loss to Auburn. He has completed 72.4% of his passes, third-best in the country, for 2,390 yards and 22 touchdowns with four interceptions. Nate Frazier has 11 rushing touchdowns, and Dwight Phillips Jr. is averaging 7.3 yards per carry.The defense has allowed 13.9 points per game, led by linebacker Chris Cole's 71 tackles and 5.5 sacks. It will be coordinated in Atlanta by a man holding two jobs: Florida State hired Glenn Schumann as its head coach on Nov. 23, but he is expected to remain with Georgia through the College Football Playoff. Schumann and Muschamp shared Georgia's coordinator title in 2022 and 2023. Now they will match wits from opposite sidelines.The Bulldogs' defense has returned to its championship form after three straight seasons of so-so production behind the line of scrimmage. The Bulldogs enter this weekend tied for ninth nationally in sacks per game (3) after ranking 117th last season.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    What to know about TexasTexas has struggled to run the ball against Georgia's defense since joining the SEC. The news gets worse: Texas is on pace to finish with its worst rushing offense since 1944.The  Longhorns have run 72 times for 83 yards in the three previous meetings against the Bulldogs: 29 yards on 27 carries in Austin, 31 on 28 in the 2024 title game and 23 on 17 in Athens last season.Sarkisian rebuilt the backfield with this game in mind, but injuries and an underperforming offensive line has made things worse. After a 2025 rushing attack that ranked 119th nationally, Texas added Hollywood Smothers from NC State and Raleek Brown from Arizona State, who had run for 939 and 1,141 yards the season before.
Smothers tore his MCL on Oct. 31 in a win against Mississippi State. Michael Terry III and Brown have carried the load since then, but the numbers haven't improved. The Longhorns didn't crack 100 yards rushing against Texas A&M, either..The Longhorns entered the final regular season game averaging 127.5 yards rushing, ranking 110th. Arch Manning has been sacked 34 times, one of the top-five worst total in the country. And the Horns continue to be without left tackle Trevor Goosby, an NFL talent who protected Manning's blind side.Simply put, Sarkisian's rebuild of the rushing game hasn't worked, but the Longhorns have survived anyway. They beat then-No. 1 Ohio State in a legendary comeback in Week 2 and won at Tennessee before back-to-back 27-24 losses to Oklahoma and Florida. Texas hasn't lost since. The Horns carry six straight victories into the SEC title game. 
Manning entered Saturday with 22 touchdown passes, tied for third in the SEC alongside Georgia's Gunner Stockton, but he also has 11 interceptions, the second-most in the conference. Still, the Longhorns own the sport's most wins against ranked teams, sitting at 5-0 before the SEC title game.The secret sauce is Muschamp's defense, which carries the Longhorns in critical moments. Colin Simmons has 10.5 sacks, tied for fifth nationally, and his 31.5 career sacks rank third in program history, but he has missed the last two games with an ankle injury. Safety Jelani McDonald, the team's leading tackler, picked off four passes in the two games before the trip to Texas A&M, the first SEC player to do that in a two-game span since 2017.Manning is 16-2 as a starter in the state Texas, but 6-3 everywhere else. "We were kinda ugly tonight," Sarkisian said after beating the Aggies on Friday.The Longhorns finished with just 242 yards, including 99 on the ground. Manning was 18 of 34 passing for a season-low 143 yards and one touchdown with one interception.
Georgia vs. Texas predictionThese teams lost three games between them this season. All three ended with 27-24 scores.The margins have been thin, but the series has not. Georgia has won three straight by smothering the Texas run game and making the Longhorns one-dimensional. Texas goes to Atlanta without its best running back and with a quarterback who has been sacked 34 times and must fend off a top-10 pass rush. Muschamp knows Smart's program as well as anyone outside Athens, and his unit is good enough to keep this close. Until Texas proves it can run on Georgia, though, the Bulldogs are the pick to close out the SEC Championship Game era with a third straight title. Prediction: Georgia wins the SEC championship and gets the No. 1 seed in the CFP.

        World Cup qualification has been secured for the United States women's national team after defeating El Salvador 8-0 on Friday in Texas. The USWNT only needed eight minutes to take the lead via Kennedy Wesley, and then the goals started rolling with NWSL MVP Ashley Sanchez securing a first-half hat trick. Sanchez helped cap off a first half that saw the USWNT score a whopping seven times before the break.Emma Hayes had to balance players being at different points of their season with the NWSL regular season coming to a close on Nov. 1 but that wouldn't stop them from getting off to a fast start despite the absence of key players for the match. Trinity Rodman was replaced on the roster by Jaedyn Shaw after picking up a shoulder injury but they didn't miss a beat.Games like this one showcase the tough decisions that Hayes will need to make as Sanchez is going to do what she can to push for a spot in a crowded attack alongside Mal Swanson, Trinity Rodman, Alyssa Thompson, and Sophia Wilson. While it's a good problem to have, as Hayes looks to build a cohesive unit between now and the World Cup she'll still want to determine who the core attack is.If they're performing like this, though, it won't matter who is starting because even both center backs got in on the fun, taking advantage of set pieces to down El Salvador in the first meeting between the two countries.
El Salvador has had a rough journey to get here with their manager Eric Acuna calling out his squad during the October international break after they lost to Paraguay. Acuna threatened to take away the players' privileges for things such as coffee while also questioning their commitment to the national team. It's a tough environment to play in, and they still tried to bring the game to the USWNT, but meeting the buzzsaw that is the second-ranked FIFA nation in the world will lead to some results like this.Getting out of the match with qualification secured and no injuries is a job well done and while Claudia Dickey didn't have to do much in net, her return to the starting goalkeeper role for the first time since the opening match against Spain could signal that Hayes has figured out what she wants to do with her rotating cast of keepers.Determining that would help set up a defense in front of them, and when Tierna Davidson and Wesley didn't allow a shot during the match while offering strong pressing moving forward, they could become a hard partnership to break up behind a balanced midfield. This is the biggest win so far under Hayes, and it begins the official road to Brazil.
Next up, there's still work to do as the USWNT will face Jamaica in the semifinals on Dec. 1 as they look to win the Concacaf W Championship and players fight for those coveted World Cup spots. The depth that Hayes has doesn't allow room for complacency, and Hayes will be the winner from that, as there is a lot to choose from on the squad, and they'll deservedly be among the favorites to win the World Cup in Brazil next summer.

title: Baylor set to hire UTSA coach Jeff Traylor after leading Roadrunners to new heights - CBS Sports
description: The former Texas high school coaching legend, who went 61-28 with three 10-win seasons at UTSA, takes over in Wac
body:
The former Texas high school coaching legend, who went 61-28 with three 10-win seasons at UTSA, takes over in Waco after Dave Aranda was fired in October
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 27, 2026

    10:27 pm ET

        Baylor is set to hire UTSA coach Jeff Traylor to the same position, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.The former Texas high school coach clinched a spot in the American Conference title game on Friday. Traylor is a legendary Texas high school football coach at Gilmer High School in East Texas, winning three state championships and earning a spot in the THSCA Hall of Honor. After stints as an assistant at Texas, SMU and Arkansas, he was named head coach at UTSA in 2020, where he helped lead the Roadrunners to an unprecedented stretch of success. The Roadrunners went 61-28 under Traylor's watch, including three 10-win seasons. They're playing for their third conference title in six years, and first since transitioning to the American in 2023. UTSA began playing football in 2011 and had never previously recorded more than 7 wins as an FBS program. Now, Traylor heads to Baylor, where he will be tasked with revitalizing a program that stagnated under former coach Dave Aranda. After winning a Big 12 title in 2021, Aranda went 22-31 with three losing seasons in five years before he was fired on Oct. 25. Each of the last three coaches at Baylor have played for a Big 12 title and won 10 games in a season. 
UTSA is set to host the American Conference Championship Game at 8 p.m. ET on Saturday at the Alamodome. It's unclear at this time whether Traylor will coach in the game, though the majority of Group of Six hires stayed with their programs last season, even after accepting new roles. Getting back to developmentAranda coached his best football with Matt Rhule's former players, but struggled to maintain the same level of recruiting and development that characterized the successes of 2019 and 2021. By hiring Traylor, the Bears are recommitting to the model that helped them reach the national elite. Traylor is regarded as one of the best Texas recruiters in America, consistently identifying developmental talent. The Roadrunners developed three NFL Draft picks during his tenure, including Pro Bowler Riq Woolen, whom he converted from wide receiver to cornerback. 
However, his developmental track record is even more impressive when considering the sheer amount of talent UTSA has lost to other programs. Last offseason alone, the Roadrunners lost 10 players to Power Four schools, including Ohio State receiver Devin McCuin and likely All-American tight end Patrick Overmyer to Houston. How good could Traylor be with the ability to retain talent? Initial questionsWhile recruiting has been his hallmark, Traylor has also been a notable identifier of coaching talent. Traylor discovered Will Stein after a stint as a high school offensive coordinator, and produced several other high-major assistants at UTSA. Building a staff will be an interesting challenge as Traylor decides what assistants to entice with high-major dollars. Offensive coordinator Rick Bowie has been a strong presence for the Roadrunners, leading the No. 33 scoring offense. Traylor will also face a critical decision regarding Baylor interim coach Joe Klanderman, who helped the Bears improve from No. 85 to No. 22 in yards-per-play defense. 
Traylor must also consider quarterback DJ Lagway, the former five-star recruit who had a promising season for the Bears after transferring in from Florida. Will he commit serious dollars to Lagway, or does he have another plan in mind? There are also a few other underclassmen who could follow Traylor to Waco, including running back Will Henderson III and wide receiver Mekhi Anderson.

title: Black Friday scorigami: Steelers-Broncos ends with final score that's never happened before in NFL history - CBS Sports
description: The Broncos and Steelers combined to make NFL history on Black Friday
body:
The Broncos and Steelers combined to make NFL history on Black Friday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Pittsburgh Steelers dealt with plenty of drama this week, but that didn't seem to slow them down on Black Friday. The Steelers destroyed the Broncos 27-5, and in the process, they made some history: This marked the first time in the NFL's 107-year history that a game has ever ended with that exact final score. The final points came in the fourth quarter when Chris Boswell hit a 33-yard field goal. That was a huge kick, because if he had missed it, a final score of 24-5 would NOT have been a scorigami, but Boswell's kick went through, and that ultimately gave us the 1,102nd final score in NFL history. 
This game featured a rare double scorigami: The Steelers led 24-5 after two quarters, marking the first time in NFL history that particular halftime score had ever occurred. For a game to end in a scorigami, you need a few bizarre things to happen, and that was certainly the case here. The biggest thing that helped the scorigami happen was that the Broncos recorded a safety in the second quarter, making the score 14-2. 
The Broncos then tacked on a Wil Lutz field goal later in the second quarter, but with Bo Nix struggling, the offense didn't score a single point for the rest of the game. When one team finishes a game with exactly five points, you're almost guaranteed to get a scorigami, and that's what happened here. The Broncos were the first team to finish with exactly five points since 2021, when the Cardinals lost a game 31-5 to the Texans (That game was also a scorigami). This game marked the first time in three years that the Broncos were involved in a scorigami. The last instance came back in November 2023 in a 29-12 loss to the Browns. On the Steelers' end, there was nothing bizarre about their point total, but their defense deserves a lot of credit for making this scorigami happen. Not only did T.J. Watt score on a fumble-return touchdown in the first quarter, but Jalen Ramsey also tacked on a pick-six in the second quarter. On top of that, the Steelers' defense had a suffocating performance against Denver, holding the Broncos out of the end zone. 
The Aaron Rodgers situation might have caused some drama in Pittsburgh this week, but there was no drama in this game. Pittsburgh's win marks the second time this month the Steelers have been involved in a scorigami. Back in Week 10, their 38-18 loss to the Bengals also made history as the first time a final score had never happened before. The Steelers are now one of four teams this year — along with the Bengals, Cowboys, and Titans — involved in multiple scorigamis.  Overall, there have been seven scorigamis this year, which is already more than we saw during the entire 2025 season (five). It's also more than we saw in 2024, when there were six in total. This is turning into the year of the scorigami.

title: Aaron Rodgers claims he was 'barred' from Steelers' facility: Why QB went scorched earth on Mike McCarthy - CBS Sports
description: Here's why the QB went scorched earth on Mike McCarthy
body:
Here's why the QB went scorched earth on Mike McCarthy
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 27, 2026

    7:15 pm ET

            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Based on how they played Friday, it seems like the Pittsburgh Steelers have already put the Aaron Rodgers drama behind them, but the same can't be said for the four-time NFL MVP. Rodgers has taken some heat this week for breaking the sanctity of the locker room and he decided to respond to that accusation by sending a text message to Al Michaels, who was on the call for Pittsburgh's Black Friday game against the Broncos. During the fourth quarter of the Amazon Prime stream, Michaels read out loud what Rodgers had sent him. "A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room," Michaels said of what Rodgers wrote. "The code or sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership. They took this public. Never heard from the head coach. Then they leaked at 11 p.m. They also barred me from the facility. That's why I went to [Pat] McAfee."
It's a short text, but there's a lot to unpack here.  For one, let's start with the fact Rodgers claims he was "barred'' from the team facility. The Steelers announced Rodgers' benching at 11:10 p.m. ET on Tuesday and they did that even though no one in the organization had actually spoken to Rodgers before the announcement came out (They did speak with his agent, though). Steelers coach Mike McCarthy made the decision to bench Rodgers after the QB gave him an ultimatum at some point on Tuesday: relinquish play-calling duties or release him. Although Rodgers didn't get released at that point, that did lead to his benching. The QB didn't show up for practice on Wednesday, and according to multiple reports, that was because the team had excused him from practice, but according to Rodgers, it was because he was banned from the facility. 
The Steelers' decision to lock Rodgers out is why he ultimately chose to talk to Pat McAfee on Wednesday. The interview was a wild ride, with Rodgers throwing out multiple accusations at Mike McCarthy, including that he had missed meetings, fallen asleep during meetings and skipped walk-throughs. Just hours after the interview with McAfee ended, Rodgers was released. During Thursday's slate of Thanksgiving games, Rodgers was called out by Tom Brady for breaking the "sanctity" of the NFL locker room, and an accusation like that from Brady likely rubbed Rodgers the wrong way, which would explain why he used Brady's wording in his text to Michaels. Based on Rodgers' claim, he may not have done the McAfee interview if he hadn't been barred from the facility, and if there had been no interview, this situation might have turned out differently. But it also seems Rodgers was determined to burn every bridge on his way out of town, so it's hard to say whether things would have turned out differently. 
Either way, the Steelers have moved on from the former quarterback and they did so in dominant fashion by beating the Denver Broncos 27-5 on Friday.

title: What's next for Ole Miss: Pete Golding faces QB, coordinator decisions after CFP hopes fade - CBS Sports
description: Ole Miss faces tough choices at quarterback and on defense after an 8-4 season fell short of lofty expectations
body:
Ole Miss faces tough choices at quarterback and on defense after an 8-4 season fell short of lofty expectations
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:28 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The first regular season of the Pete Golding era ended in a 41-17 win over in-state rival Mississippi State in a game that looked closer than the final score. Ole Miss, which started the season ranked No. 9, finished 8-4 and will miss the College Football Playoff. Golding's debut season may be best remembered for what could have been in Trinidad Chambliss' final season in Oxford. There were high highs like a dramatic win over former coach Lane Kiffin on Sept. 19. There were low lows like a blowout loss to Florida and a playoff dream-killing road loss at Oklahoma. Given the expectations, the season could be considered a disappointment and yet not an outright failure. What's next for Ole Miss? These are the big questions to consider.Who takes over defensive play-calling?Golding has already announced that he'll be passing off the defensive play-calling to someone else next season. It was a mistake for Golding, a first-time head coach, to try to balance both jobs from the jump. There's a reason even Golding's former boss, Nick Saban, wasn't calling defensive plays at Alabama, though he was heavily involved in game planning and strategic decisions. At least it only took a season for Golding to realize he erred there. 
The name that industry sources have mentioned the most for the role is Arkansas defensive coordinator Ron Roberts. The connection is obvious, given that Golding and Roberts have known each other for more than two decades, dating back to their shared time at Delta State. Still, Roberts has bounced around the last few years and is on his third SEC defensive coordinator job since 2023. At Arkansas this season, Roberts' defense ranks 81st in total defense, 88th in pass defense and 92nd in scoring defense. If Cal moves on from first-year coach Tosh Lupoi, he is another name who could get traction for the job. Lupoi and Golding worked together for a season under Saban at Alabama. Lupoi's job security has been in question amidst a 3-8 debut season. Whomever Golding hires for the position, it needs to be someone he trusts enough that he won't be tempted to micromanage and yank the defensive play-calling responsibilities back. It would help the next defensive coordinator to retain Suntarine Perkins, too. 
Who starts at quarterback?Let's start with the obvious: Ole Miss is going to miss Trinidad Chambliss. The terrific quarterback regressed a bit in 2026 and was more turnover-prone, but still had dazzling big-play ability that was frequently there when Ole Miss needed it most. Replacing him won't be easy. Deuce Knight makes the most sense as an in-house replacement. The former five-star recruit has only thrown 43 passes in his collegiate career, however. The Ole Miss coaching staff has had a season to get an up-close look at what Knight brings to the table. Is what Knight has done in practice enough to turn the offense over to him? And, if so, at what cost? If Ole Miss prefers a veteran option out of the transfer portal, the pool may be limited. There are more teams that need a transfer QB than there are viable starting quarterbacks available. And the absolute best ones could cost in the neighborhood of what Mississippi State quarterback Kamario Taylor got ($6 million). 
Ole Miss showed with Chambliss that it is willing to spend big on a top quarterback. But if you spend $5 million on just an average quarterback, it can sink your roster because of the opportunity cost of where that money could have gone. Retaining Knight at a reasonable cost, noting the lack of college production, could be helpful not only for trying to also keep players like receiver Deuce Alexander but also for adding more offensive weapons.That's a separate question about whether offensive coordinator John David Baker is the right guy to be feeding the play calls into the QB's helmet, but that's a whole different discussion. What should expectations be?With Chambliss and running back Kewan Lacy coming back for 2026, it was reasonable to expect Ole Miss to return to the playoff for a second consecutive season. That's not happening.
But the expectation should be the same in 2027, especially with the playoff expanding to 24 teams. With how Ole Miss finished this season at 8-4, that would be enough to make the playoff next season. Perhaps it is unfair to put the same playoff-level expectations on a team that doesn't have Chambliss at quarterback, but Lane Kiffin raised the bar in his time in Oxford. If Golding can nail the right defensive coordinator and quarterback decisions, Ole Miss should be in that 8-9 win range again in 2027. The Rebels have an easy non-conference slate that should lead to a 3-0 start. If Ole Miss has any chance of meeting expectations, it will need to win games against Mississippi State, Arkansas and South Carolina, too. And then it comes down to whether Golding can win two or three games against this group: Alabama, Kentucky, Oklahoma, at LSU, at Tennessee and at Texas A&M. 
If he can't, the disappointment of what could have been for 2026 will turn to increased frustration and angst.

title: NFL Week 12 injury report: Brock Purdy, Justin Herbert out as QB health dwindles across league - CBS Sports

Final injury reports for every team playing on Sunday in Week 12

        About one-third of the NFL will operate with backup quarterbacks in Week 12 as an injury plague continues to ravage the position league-wide. This year has seen a carousel of quarterbacks and a near record number of starters, and two more teams will join the list of squads that have had to insert a No. 2 signal-caller into the starting lineup.The San Francisco 49ers will be without an MVP contender on Sunday as Brock Purdy deals with an ankle injury that occurred in last week's win over the Minnesota Vikings. Coach Kyle Shanahan said this week that it is not a high ankle sprain, which is good news, but he did not practice at all in the lead-up to the NFC West battle against the Seattle Seahawks. Mac Jones, who is widely regarded as a top-flight backup, is in line to make his first start of the year.And in Southern California, an already dismal Los Angeles Chargers offense could become even more ineffective with Justin Herbert ruled out for the contest against the New England Patriots. The worst offense in the league by EPA per play is poised to insert DJ Uiagalelei into action for the first start of his career.The silver lining for the Chargers is that the Patriots will also trot out a backup in Tommy DeVito.
These signal-caller ailments amount to the highest-profile absences of Week 12, but other standouts will miss time when Sunday rolls around, too. Here are the final injury reports for every team playing this weekend.Odds via DraftKings SportsbookSaints at Bengals (-10)Saints: TE Juwan Johnson (hamstring, wrist) OUT; TE Noah Fant (calf), T Taliese Fuaga (knee), T Asim Richards (knee) QUESTIONABLEBengals: G Dalton Risner (knees) OUT; CB Jalen Davis (hamstring) DOUBTFUL; WR Tee Higgins (hamstring), WR Andrei Iosivas (thumb) QUESTIONABLEThe tight end group in New Orleans is in rough shape with at least one of the top receiving threats in that unit poised to miss Week 12. Juwan Johnson has been a focal point in the passing game throughout Kellen Moore's coaching tenure and will sit this week after he left the last game with a hamstring issue, and Noah Fant is no guarantee to suit up following his limited participation in Friday's practice.Tee Higgins popped up on the injury report on Friday after he woke up with hamstring soreness, but coach Zac Taylor said the situation is "not a concern" and that the star receiver is expected to play. Dalton Risner, on the other hand, is out for a second consecutive week with knee injuries but is day-to-day, which suggests he will be poised to return when the Bengals take on the Browns next week. Jalen Rivers will man the right guard duties in his absence.
Giants at Colts (+6)Giants: DE Shelby Harris (illness) OUTColts: TE Will Mallory (hamstring), RB Seth McGowan (hamstring), DT Jerry Tillery (calf), T Jalen Travis (knee), CB Charvarius Ward (knee) OUT; TE Andrew Ogletree (knee), CB Cam Taylor-Britt (groin) QUESTIONABLEThe interior of the Giants defensive line will be a touch lighter than usual as Shelby Harris sits out with an illness, but the rest of the front is at full strength as edge rusher Abdul Carter and linebacker Arvell Reese avoided injury designations. Reese practiced in full on Friday, and Carter was a limited participant after he missed the Wednesday and Thursday sessions.Indianapolis' secondary is in rough shape. Sauce Gardner will return to the lineup, but with Charvarius Ward out and Cam Taylor-Britt's availability to be determined, the Giants could be in for a big day through the air against this defense. Stopping Cam Skattebo on the ground will also be a challenge for the Colts with Jerry Tillery on the sideline.Jets at Dolphins (+5.5)Jets: WR Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle/groin) OUT; DL David Onyemata (abdomen), DL Harrison Phillips (ankle), DL T'Vondre Sweat (knee) QUESTIONABLEDolphins: CB Julius Brents (neck/shoulder), P Bradley Pinion (right groin), WR Jared Wayne (quad) OUT; LB Ronnie Harrison (hamstring) QUESTIONABLEA stop-and-start rookie season for Omar Cooper Jr. continues with his sixth absence and second in as many weeks. The Jets still own a number of weapons around quarterback Geno Smith and last week enjoyed an unforeseen two-touchdown effort from veteran Sterling Shepard in Cooper's absence. The trio of defensive linemen on the injury report could be an issue for a beleaguered defense that surrendered 28 points in a loss to the Dolphins in Week 7.
The Dolphins have done a whole lot of punting during their one-win season. When they do so in Week 12, it will be Jack Browning handling those duties with Bradley Pinion out due to the groin injury he suffered on his final punt a week ago. Browning is a former college walk-on who bounced around rosters as an undrafted rookie, made five appearances with the Buccaneers and even spent a year in the UFL.Falcons at Vikings (-7)Falcons: OL Matthew Bergeron (back), CB Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring), WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring), WR Jahan Dotson (hamstring), S DeMarcco Hellams (foot) OUTVikings: WR Jordan Addison (thumb), OT Christian Darrisaw (shoulder), CB Isaiah Rodgers (thigh) OUT; FS Harrison Smith (thigh) QUESTIONABLEWide receiver depth behind Drake London is limited with Zachariah Branch and Jahan Dotson both ruled out. The next most productive wideout available is Olamide Zaccheaus, who has just eight catches on the year. The Falcons figure to lean heavily on their running backs and tight end Kyle Pitts to pick up the slack.The Kirk Cousins-led offense is still not quite at full strength in Minnesota as Jordan Addison remains out as he recovers from thumb surgery. Coach Kevin O'Connell said this week that the No. 2 receiver is "progressing well," but it will be at least another week until he returns. Addison hurt his thumb in practice on Nov. 13. Defensively, the Vikings' elite unit might have to operate without the anchor of its secondary in Smith since he missed the first two days of practice and was a limited participant on Friday.
Titans at Jaguars (-14)Titans: S Terrell Burgess (knee), CB Cordale Flott (neck) OUT; G Fernando Carmona (ankle), T Dan Moore Jr. (knee) QUESTIONABLEJaguars: RB Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot), WR Parker Washington (shoulder), DE BJ Green II (forearm), OT Patrick Mekari (back) OUT; C Robert Hainsey (knee) QUESTIONABLEThe Jaguars own a plethora of capable wide receivers and need them to step up with Parker Washington on the shelf. Washington injured the AC joint in one of his shoulders during practice on Thursday and is week-to-week. They will also lean on their running back depth since Bhayshul Tuten will miss at least one game following his aggravation of an ankle injury in last Sunday's loss. Chris Rodriguez Jr. has been a productive No. 2 ballcarrier all year and could thrive in an expanded role.Dan Moore Jr. was a non-participant on Wednesday and only practiced in a limited fashion the following two days, so the Titans could be preparing to shake up their offensive line as their starting left tackle enters the weekend with a "questionable" designation. If he cannot play, Tennessee could be in trouble against a loaded Jaguars defensive front capable of rattling Cam Ward.Ravens at Texans (-6.5)Ravens: S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee), G Olaivavega Ioane (hand), DL Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) OUTTexans: WR Kayshon Boutte (hip), DE Danielle Hunter (hamstring), TE Brevin Jordan (finger/foot), G Keylan Rutledge (neck/shoulder) OUT; LB Jacob Hummel (abdomen/groin) QUESTIONABLEThis is the second absence of the year for Olaivavega Ioane and is related to a hand injury he sustained during Thursday's practice. The promising rookie lineman's exclusion from the lineup is just the latest blow to a Ravens interior offensive line that has been an issue over the last couple of seasons, and with this season slipping away, it is untimely. If the shakeup in the trenches hampers Baltimore against the stout Houston front and factors into a loss, the Ravens' campaign will effectively be over.
Speaking of that ferocious Texans defensive line, Danielle Hunter missing a third consecutive game strips Houston of half of an elite pass-rushing tandem with Defensive Player of the Year candidate Will Anderson Jr. This is as much of a must-win game for the Texans as it is for the Ravens, so his extended absence is also ill-timed. Meanwhile, at wide receiver, Houston boasts great depth and should be able to overcome Kayshon Boutte's hip issue.Patriots at Chargers (+2.5)Patriots: WR A.J. Brown (hamstring), CB Carlton Davis III (knee), QB Drake Maye (fibula), WR Romeo Doubs (shoulder) OUT; DT Christian Barmore (knee), FB Reggie Gilliam (knee), OL Walter Rouse (concussion protocol), G Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring QUESTIONABLEChargers: LB Daiyan Henley (knee), QB Justin Herbert (concussion), RB Keaton Mitchell (knee) OUT; LB Akheem Mesidor (ankle), WR Brenen Thompson (hamstring) DOUBTFUL; TE David Njoku (shoulder), CB Tarheem Still (ankle), DE Dalvin Tomlinson (knee), LB Tuli Tuipulotu (ankle), S Kendall Williamson (calf) QUESTIONABLESunday marks Tommy DeVito's insertion into the starting lineup as the Patriots' starting quarterback while Drake Maye begins an indefinite absence with a fractured fibula. DeVito entered New England's last game on the opening drive when Maye suffered the injury and oversaw a pitiful offensive showing en route to a blowout loss to the Lions on international soil, but with a bye week to prepare for his first start, perhaps DeVito will fare better against the lowly Chargers. He will be without a number of weapons around him, though, as the Patriots remain one of the most injury-riddled teams in the NFL.This is a backup vs. backup game at the quarterback position since the Chargers will also debut a new signal-caller. DJ Uiagalelei is poised to fill in for Justin Herbert, who is out with a concussion. An already awful year for the Los Angeles offense could get even worse.
Commanders at Cardinals (+6.5)Commanders: CB Amik Robertson (ankle) OUTCardinals: QB Carson Beck (back), G Jon Gaines II (ankle), DT Zachary Carter (knee) OUT; LB Cody Simon (calf), TE Hunter Long (ankle), LB Karson Sharar (groin) QUESTIONABLEThe number of key Commanders on injured reserve is brutal, but at least most everyone on the active roster will be available come Sunday. All but Amik Robertson practiced in full on Friday. The starting slot cornerback did not play last week, either.It is another week of Josh Johnson atop the Cardinals offense as Carson Beck continues to nurse the back issue that held him out last week. Neither quarterback has won a game as the starter this year, but Beck owns more upside than the 40-year-old Johnson and figures to return to the lineup once healthy so the Cardinals can gauge whether the rookie has a future in the league. Coach Mike LaFleur said this week that the team needs to identify a better plan for Beck's recovery moving forward.Seahawks at 49ers (-3)Seahawks: T Abraham Lucas (ankle), G Quenton Nelson (knee), NT Jarran Reed (toe) OUT49ers: QB Brock Purdy (ankle), WR Jordan Watkins (groin) OUT; WR Mike Evans (Achilles), LB Dre Greenlaw (neck), DB Siran Neal (knee, foot), OL Austen Pleasants (knee), CB Upton Stout (shoulder, neck) QUESTIONABLESam Darnold is ready to return to the Seahawks offense after he missed the last two games. Although Drew Lock managed the offense at a high level and remains unbeaten as a fill-in starter this year, coach Mike Macdonald made it clear that the starting job is Darnold's. He could not return for a more meaningful game since Seattle has a chance to take down the ailing, NFC West-leading 49ers in a rematch of the Week 5 classic that went San Francisco's way.
Situations like this are exactly why the 49ers valued Mac Jones so greatly in the offseason and at the trade deadline. Owning one of the NFL's most renowned backup quarterbacks is a luxury. The litany of injuries across this roster have not yet proved costly thanks to immense depth at all positions, and this may be another case of the 49ers being as stocked as anyone. Either that or they will feel the impact of losing an MVP-caliber quarterback for at least a week and suffer just their second loss of the year.Raiders at Browns (-4.5)Raiders: DT Adam Butler (concussion), DT Tonka Hemingway (stinger), DT Tim Keenan III (knee), G/C Jackson Powers-Johnson (Achilles) OUT; TE Brock Bowers (ankle), DE Patrick Johnson (stinger), DT JJ Pegues (elbow), CB Darrell Luter Jr. (knee) QUESTIONABLEBrowns: DE Derek Barnett (hamstring) OUT; OT Austin Barber (knee), WR Denzel Boston (quad), RB Raheim Sanders (hip) QUESTIONABLEBrock Bowers did not participate in the Raiders' Friday practice, which is a concerning development after he practiced in a limited fashion the previous two days. It could have been a rest day, but the star tight end may also have sustained a setback in his recovery from the ankle issue that held him out last week. Rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza moved the ball quite well even without the Raiders' primary receiving threat a week ago but would undoubtedly benefit greatly from Bowers' return should he make his way back into the lineup on "Sunday Night Football."One of the top offensive rookies in the league is in danger of missing his first game. Denzel Boston suffered a quad injury last week and is questionable for "SNF." Browns coach Todd Monken said the coaching staff pushed him "pretty hard" early in the week, pulled back on Friday and will know more about his status on Saturday when they conduct a walkthrough. If he cannot go, fellow rookie KC Concepcion could see an uptick in targets. The offense may also have to operate without its starting right guard, Austin Barber, although he is trending in the right direction as a limited participant in Friday's practice.

title: Former lottery pick Rob Dillingham sucker-punched in G League game, leading to scrum, multiple ejections - CBS Sports
description: Dillingham, the No. 8 pick in 2024, is trying to work his way back to the NBA
body:
Dillingham, the No. 8 pick in 2024, is trying to work his way back to the NBA
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 27, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:20 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Former No. 8 overall pick Rob Dillingham was sucker-punched by Felix Okpara during a G League game between the Westchester Knicks and Capital City Go-Go on Friday afternoon. Dillingham and Okpara were both ejected after the incident, which turned into a full-on scrum that spilled off the court. Dillingham, who was traded to the New York Knicks' G League affiliate earlier this month, pushed Okpara in the chest as the two were running up the floor early in the fourth quarter. Okpara looked around to see if an official had seen what happened, waited a few seconds, then unleashed a haymaker on Dillingham. 
Dillingham was knocked down, but got to his feet quickly and chased after Okpara, who retreated immediately. Players, officials, coaches, team executives and security all rushed in to separate the two, and the situation eventually calmed down without any further issues. Both players are likely to face additional punishment beyond their ejections. Okpara, in particular, is almost certainly facing a suspension. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dillingham in G League looking for another chanceThe Minnesota Timberwolves traded an unprotected 2031 first-round pick and a 2030 pick swap to the San Antonio Spurs for the No. 8 overall pick in the 2024 NBA Draft, which they used to select Dillingham out of the University of Kentucky, where he had an impressive freshman season. Dillingham, 21, never got much of a chance in Minnesota, however, in large part because the Timberwolves were trying to contend -- they went to the Western Conference Finals in his rookie season -- and weren't in a position to let him play through mistakes. He played just 84 games in a season and a half with the Timberwolves before he was traded to the Chicago Bulls as part of the Ayo Dosunmu deal. In 30 games with the Bulls, Dillingham got a much bigger opportunity, but failed to impress. He averaged 9.6 points on 50.3% true shooting in 21.5 minutes, and had an 18.3% turnover rate. Notably, he shot just 30% from 3-point range, when outside shooting was supposed to be one of his primary strengths coming out of college. 
The Bulls traded Dillingham to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield in September ahead of training camp, and the Hornets waived him a day later. On Nov. 13, the Westchester Knicks acquired the returning player rights to Dillingham from the Iowa Wolves, in exchange for the returning player rights to Tuburu Naivalurua, Westchester's own future first-round pick and a 2027 second-round pick in the G League Draft. Dillingham put up 26 points and six assists on 10 of 18 from the field, including 3 of 5 from 3-point range, in his debut on Nov. 20. Entering Friday's contest, he was averaging 21 points and 6.3 assists, while shooting 35.3% from behind the arc. 
"I ain't really trying to show too much of anything to anyone or prove to anyone, it's more internal," Dillingham told SNY ahead of his debut. "Showing myself that I can play basketball at the highest level, fit into any situation and help. "I want everyone to see that I'm better at these things, for sure, but that's not my goal. If you focus on that, then you're going to lose focus on what you're really trying to do.  Focused on myself, getting better, so when I get the opportunity, I'm ready and improved."

        Aaron Rodgers is such a transcendent figure in the sports world that he has been a staple in popular culture throughout his two-decade career. Like many of the most memorable moments from his NFL tenure, his release from the Pittsburgh Steelers and scathing comments about coach Mike McCarthy this week made waves outside just the football community. St. John's basketball coach Rick Pitino even caught wind of the drama and took a jab at Rodgers while talking about his squad on Friday.St. John's defeated Iowa State in the Players Era 16 college basketball tournament on Black Friday, and in his assessment of the victory, Pitino credited his players' intangibles and took a not-so-subtle shot at Rodgers in the process."You can't teach class, and you can't teach character," Pitino said. "You saw that on the football screen the other day."Rodgers accused McCarthy of arriving late to team activities or missing them altogether, sleeping through an offensive meeting and breaking down the locker room on one occasion during last week's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles with "1-2-3 Packers."

        
            
                Former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin on Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy saga: 'It's a dumpster fire'
                
                    Jordan Dajani                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
References to Rodgers' handling of his benching and eventual release have been widespread throughout the sports universe. During the Steelers' first game since the stunning turn of events, the Denver Broncos trolled them as they celebrated a safety. Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton broke out Rodgers' signature "discount double-check" celebration when he stuffed running back Jaylen Warren in the end zone for two points.And on Thanksgiving, another future Hall of Famer called out Rodgers for his antics. Tom Brady disapproved of Rodgers making private matters public.
"The sanctity of an NFL locker room is a very sacred place, and we should never lose track of that as players," Brady said during the broadcast of Thursday's Dallas Cowboys vs. Eagles game. "It's a privilege to be in that locker room. You're fighting with your teammates. You're fighting coaches. You're always acting as a team together. It shouldn't always be the place for private things to become public; that's what I'll say."

title: Mason Rudolph and Steelers defense can clean up Aaron Rodgers' mess, but the franchise's problems run deeper - CBS Sports

body:
Well, of course Mason Rudolph was the answer.Days after Aaron Rodgers set fire to the place on his way out of town, the Steelers turned to the same quarterback who rescued their season three years ago. And against a Broncos team that came to Pittsburgh with eight wins and legitimate Super Bowl aspirations, the Steelers were unequivocally the better football team.So now what? Is this a dead-cat-bounce win for a team that just endured Aaron Rodgers Armageddon, or is there something here? And if the Broncos can entertain thoughts of winning a Super Bowl with what they've gotten out of Bo Nix this season, why can't the Steelers make something of their remaining season with Rudolph?And after all that's happened, the Steelers are somehow 7-4. If you squint, there are reasons to believe they can make something of this season. There are also reasons, if you're clear-headed and rational, to be concerned about what another nine- or 10-win season might mean for an organization that has spent years mistaking winning for progress.Maybe the Steelers found a way to salvage a season that, 48 hours ago, felt unsalvageable. What they can't afford to do is mistake that for having figured out their future.
If the Broncos can do it, why can't the Steelers?We've previously written about the Broncos, whose ability to win close games has been unprecedented. They've done it despite routinely getting outgained and despite uneven play from Nix.But here's the thing: Coming into their Black Friday matchup, the Steelers had played better defense than the Broncos, hadn't been outgained by anything close to 700 yards and hadn't needed nearly as many late-game heroics to win. The Broncos had two more victories to show for it, but there wasn't nearly as much separating these teams as their records might suggest.Steelers vs. Broncos entering Week 12SteelersBroncosRecord6-48-2Point differential+13+26Yardage differential-39-718Offensive EPA-28.8-6.0Defensive EPA+39.9+16.2Points allowed/game20.121.0Special teams EPA+1.9+15.8One-score record4-26-0Nix had been playing considerably better of late. After an underwhelming first six games, he was averaging 52 more passing yards per game and had thrown six touchdowns against two interceptions over his next four starts. Denver won all four games, scoring at least 26 points each time.Friday served as a reminder of just how much Denver needs Nix to take care of the football. One of his greatest strengths coming into the season was his ability to avoid sacks, which helped offset his inability to consistently generate big plays. The Steelers defense turned a Nix sack-fumble and a pick-six into 14 points in the first half alone. When it was over, Patrick Graham's group had sacked Nix twice and held him to 169 passing yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions.Pittsburgh has a defense capable of doing that to opposing QBs. The question, as it has been for the better part of eight seasons, is whether the Steelers' own quarterback situation can overcome replacement-level play.What can the Steelers realistically expect from Rudolph?Nobody's confusing Rudolph with anything more than a reliable journeyman backup. They need him to be better than Aaron Rodgers, which, despite everything Rodgers accomplished in his first two decades in the league, was immediately obvious on Friday.And it's worth remembering what Rudolph did the last time the Steelers found themselves in such a predicament. In his three regular-season starts in 2023, he averaged more than 10 yards per attempt, threw three touchdowns without an interception and won all three games. Nobody benefited more from Rudolph's willingness to push the ball downfield than George Pickens.QBYards/attemptEPA/dropbackRudolph, 202310.1+0.19Rudolph, career entering Friday6.7-0.03Nix, 2026 entering Friday6.1-0.00Rodgers, 20266.2-0.12Reprising the role of Pickens on Friday: DK Metcalf!On Friday, Rudolph completed 9 of 15 passes for 142 yards, including a 58-yarder to rookie Germie Bernard, a 37-yarder to Roman Wilson and a 22-yard touchdown to the aforementioned Mr. Metcalf. Given what the Steelers have invested in their wide receivers and how little they've gotten in return, it'll be worth watching whether Rudolph can consistently get more out of that group than Rodgers did.Here's where it gets dangerous for the SteelersIf Rudolph can do for the Steelers what he did back in '23, it's reasonable to think that, yes, this group will make the playoffs – and, yes, will be underdogs to actually win a playoff game. The bigger concern, however, is how the organization might interpret that success given the last decade.Because we've been here before. Three years ago, the Steelers were 6-4, had set the forward-passing game back decades, and eventually turned to Mason Rudolph to save their season. Since then, they've changed coordinators and head coaches, completely overhauled their quarterback room (twice), and committed $209 million to two of the NFL's least productive wide receivers (whether due to injury or inconsistency).And what do they have to show for it? Consider this: Of the 133 NFL teams to start 6-4 since 2000, only three were less efficient throwing the football than the '26 Steelers: the 2000 Lions, the 2022 Jets and … the aforementioned 2023 Steelers (as measured by EPA per dropback).Expand that group to include seven previous teams that started 6-4 and also really struggled to throw the ball, and here's what happened: Not a single, solitary one of them improved its record the following season. In fact, together they won just 35% of their games, and four of those seven lost at least 12 times.And what did those franchises do in the seasons that followed? Some found their way out of the dysfunction; others made decisions that would haunt them for years—and, in some cases, decades.6-4 teams with struggling passing offenses, 2000-25TeamEPA/DB (10 games)Final record1 year later2 years later3 years later4 years later2000 Lions-0.149-72-143-135-116-102003 Dolphins-0.1110-64-129-76-101-152016 Texans-0.079-74-1211-510-64-122017 Titans-0.109-79-79-711-512-52022 Patriots-0.098-94-134-1314-3--2022 Jets-0.137-107-105-123-14--2023 Steelers-0.2010-710-710-7----2026 Steelers-0.12TBD--------Teams since 2000 that started 6-4 with an EPA/dropback of -0.07 or worse.How bad can it get? Ask the DolphinsIn 2003, four years removed from Dan Marino's retirement, Miami had Ricky Williams in the backfield and a defense that featured Jason Taylor, Zach Thomas, Junior Seau, Patrick Surtain and Sam Madison. Dave Wannstedt's team won 10 games with Jay Fiedler and Brian Griese at quarterback. The Dolphins missed the playoffs, but it's not difficult to understand why they might have thought they were a quarterback away.They traded a future second-round pick for AJ Feeley, who threw 15 interceptions in eight starts in 2004. Williams abruptly retired, Wannstedt resigned and the Dolphins won four games. Enter Nick Saban, who got them back to 9-7 in his first season with Gus Frerotte.And then came perhaps the most consequential personnel decision of the century for the Dolphins: In March 2006, Miami passed on Drew Brees, who was coming off shoulder surgery, and traded a second-round pick for Daunte Culpepper, who was recovering from a serious knee injury.Saban has since said he wanted Brees, but the Dolphins' doctors wouldn't clear him. Either way, Culpepper started four games for Miami, Brees spent the next 15 seasons in New Orleans, and Saban was in Tuscaloosa less than a year later. The Dolphins went 1-15 in 2007.It can get even worse -- just ask the LionsThen there's Detroit, which replaced longtime executive Chuck Schmidt with Matt Millen following its nine-win season in 2000. Millen hired Marty Mornhinweg; the Lions won two games, and a year later they drafted Joey Harrington with the third overall pick. Detroit drafted a wide receiver in the first round in each of the next three years: Charles Rogers, Roy Williams and Mike Williams.The Lions went 31-97 from 2001-2008, including a 0-16 finish in Millen's final season. They finally got it right at quarterback, drafting Matthew Stafford first overall in 2009, but went 74-90-1 in his starts over 12 seasons and never won a playoff game. Stafford won a Super Bowl in his first season after Detroit traded him to the Rams in 2021, and the Lions finally figured it out after hiring GM Brad Holmes and head coach Dan Campbell. With Jared Goff, Detroit went from three wins in 2021 to nine in 2022 to 12 and an NFC Championship game appearance in 2023. Detroit won more playoff games that season (two) than it had in the previous 65 seasons combined (one).The Steelers should be very familiar with what happened to the JetsThe 2022 Jets had the NFL's fourth-ranked scoring defense, both the Offensive and Defensive Rookies of the Year in Garrett Wilson and Sauce Gardner … and a problem at quarterback. Former No. 2 overall pick Zach Wilson didn't come close to living up to his draft status, and Robert Saleh's team went 1-6 down the stretch.General manager Joe Douglas traded for Rodgers, the Jets hired Nathaniel Hackett as offensive coordinator and brought in some of Rodgers' former teammates. Rodgers tore his Achilles in the opener, New York won seven games – just as they had the season before – and they doubled down the following offseason, eventually trading for Davante Adams.The Jets did improve throwing the football in 2024. The defense, meanwhile, went from one of the league's best to a liability. They won five games, fired Saleh and Douglas, moved on from Rodgers and won three games in 2025.This should sound familiar. One difference: Gardner, Wilson, Quinnen Williams and Breece Hall were all 25 or younger when New York first decided they were just a QB away. Pittsburgh doesn't have that luxury with T.J. Watt, Cameron Heyward and Jalen Ramsey.There are ways out of thisBill O'Brien's Texans won exactly nine games in each of his first three seasons as head coach. Houston gave Brock Osweiler $72 million in 2016; he threw more interceptions than touchdowns, and general manager Rick Smith spent the following offseason getting himself out of the mess.The Texans attached a second-round pick to Osweiler to get Cleveland to take his contract, then gave the Browns two first-rounders to move from No. 25 to No. 12 to draft Deshaun Watson. Watson tore his ACL as a rookie, but Houston won 21 games and two division titles over the next two seasons.
Tennessee didn't have to spend nearly as much. The Titans parted ways with Mike Mularkey after winning a playoff game in January 2018, hired Mike Vrabel and, a year later, GM Jon Robinson got to work.He traded for Ryan Tannehill, ostensibly to back up Marcus Mariota, signed guard Rodger Saffold and drafted Jeffery Simmons, AJ Brown and four-year starting guard Nate Davis with his first three picks. Vrabel promoted Arthur Smith to offensive coordinator, Tannehill replaced Mariota in October of the '19 season and the Titans were playing for a trip to the Super Bowl three months later.The other example is New England, which appeared to have found Tom Brady's successor in Mac Jones, the 15th overall pick in 2021. Jones made the Pro Bowl and led the Patriots to the playoffs as a rookie before Bill Belichick, in a peculiar display of hubris, entrusted his offense to a longtime defensive coordinator (Matt Patricia) and his young quarterback's development to a former special teams coordinator (Joe Judge). Jones never recovered in New England, and both he and Kenny Pickett, whom the Steelers drafted 20th overall a year later, were traded in March 2024.
The Patriots endured consecutive four-win seasons, drafted Drake Maye third overall, hired Vrabel and Josh McDaniels, and added Will Campbell, TreVeyon Henderson and Stefon Diggs. They won 14 games in 2025 and went to the Super Bowl.So what exactly are the Steelers building?Really, the Steelers have been trying to solve some variation of the same problem since 2019, when Ben Roethlisberger suffered a season-ending elbow injury in Week 2. In six of the eight seasons since, they've had a below-average offense through 10 games, and in five of those seasons, their passing game actually cost them points (at least as measured by EPA per dropback).Perhaps Mike Tomlin's greatest accomplishment over his final seven seasons in Pittsburgh was his ability to hold together a team that was frequently overmatched offensively. Whatever your criticisms of Tomlin -- and there were plenty of legitimate ones -- there's something to be said for consistently winning with the quarterbacks he had. McCarthy inherited many of those same problems, and we're beginning to see what happens when the head coach can no longer paper over them.SeasonThru 10 gamesOFF EPAPASS EPA/DB20195-5-79.56-0.111202010-0+13.71+0.09220215-4-1-13.90-0.03520223-7-55.01-0.12020236-4-65.37-0.19920248-2-24.57+0.04320256-4+3.92+0.02820266-4-28.83-0.115We've written plenty about Pittsburgh's recent struggles in the draft, the decision to pay DK Metcalf $150 million and trade George Pickens and whether the organization's obsession with avoiding a losing season has done more long-term harm than short-term good.They're not unrelated. The organization spent recent years making personnel decisions as if it had the franchise QB on the roster. They've committed big money to veteran receivers, and four players they selected in the first three rounds from 2022 through 2025 -- Pickett, George Pickens, Broderick Jones and Kaleb Johnson -- have all been traded away.GM Omar Khan has drafted some good young players, but how much longer can Pittsburgh operate under the assumption that it's only a competent quarterback away from winning its first playoff game since the 2016 season?The last time Pittsburgh had a losing season? It was 2003, and a few months later, it drafted Ben Roethlisberger. That doesn't mean another losing season guarantees another Big Ben, any more than drafting Joey Harrington guaranteed Detroit anything.And there's nothing wrong with Rudolph helping this team win 10 games. There is something wrong with using that as justification for another offseason of the same decisions that got us here in the first place.But the danger isn't going 6-11. As we wrote back in January, after Tomlin retired, the Steelers entered the offseason with the NFL's second-oldest roster, $46.6 million in cap space and 12 draft picks. It was an opportunity to get younger, accumulate more draft capital by moving some veteran players and build a roster capable of supporting their next franchise QB. Instead, the Steelers doubled down on winning now despite little evidence they were close to winning anything meaningful. The danger is continuing to operate as if they're close to winning a Super Bowl when they're much closer to being a bad football team with an expensive roster and no quarterback.The Dolphins thought they were a quarterback away, too. That was more than 20 years ago, and they're still waiting to win another playoff game.
